html:
Buddhism is a religion and way of life founded by Siddhartha Gautama, the Buddha, in the Ganges plain of northern India around the 5th century BCE. It has roughly half a billion followers today, mostly in East, Southeast and South Asia.

Its core teaching: life is marked by suffering caused by craving; craving can end; and the way to end it is the Eightfold Path of right understanding, conduct and meditation. Beings are reborn according to their karma until they reach nirvana, release from the cycle. The community of monks and nuns, the sangha, carried the teaching on.

How it spread:

  • The Mauryan emperor Ashoka backed it in the 200s BCE and sent missions abroad, including to Sri Lanka.
  • Along the Silk Road it reached China in the 1st century CE, then Korea, and Japan in the 500s, where Prince Shōtoku championed it.
  • Chinese monks such as Xuanzang went to India to bring back texts.

Two main branches formed: Theravada in Sri Lanka and Southeast Asia, and Mahayana in East Asia, which gave rise to schools such as the Pure Land and Zen. Vajrayana grew in Tibet.

In China it had times of favour, as under Wu Zetian, and of persecution. In India it faded after about 1200, but in 1956 B. R. Ambedkar led hundreds of thousands of Dalits into it (Ambedkar's mass conversion).
sum: Buddhism is a religion and way of life founded by Siddhartha Gautama, the Buddha, in the Ganges plain of northern India around the 5th century BCE. It has roughly half a billion followers today, mostly in East, Southeast and South Asia.
